title: Jordan Elise Navarro
biography_text:
Jordan Elise Navarro (born 14 March 1988) is a Nonprofit Program Manager known for designing and overseeing community-based education and health initiatives. Navarro has worked with regional and city-level nonprofit organizations, focusing on youth development, digital literacy, and access to basic health services. Their work centers on planning, coordinating, and evaluating programs that serve low-income neighborhoods.

Navarro was born in the small coastal city of Harbor Point. They grew up in a bilingual household and attended local public schools. During secondary school, Navarro volunteered at a community center, where they assisted with homework clubs and weekend food distributions. This early experience with organized service activities later influenced their decision to work in the nonprofit sector.

Navarro earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology from North Shore Metropolitan University. While at the university, they completed internships with two local nonprofits that focused on youth mentoring and housing support. Navarro later obtained a Master of Public Administration degree with a concentration in nonprofit management. Their graduate studies emphasized program design, budgeting, and outcome measurement for social service organizations.

After completing their education, Navarro accepted an entry-level position at Harbor Youth Alliance, a small nonprofit that provided after-school activities. They initially worked as a program assistant, helping with scheduling, sign-in procedures, and data entry. Within three years, Navarro was promoted to Nonprofit Program Manager. In this role, they supervised a team of coordinators, managed grant-funded projects, and ensured that each program followed safety and reporting requirements.

As a Nonprofit Program Manager at Harbor Youth Alliance, Navarro created a structured homework support program, a weekend robotics club, and a leadership workshop series for teenagers. They developed written curricula, trained volunteers, and established partnerships with local schools. Navarro also introduced a system for tracking attendance and academic outcomes, which helped the organization secure additional funding from regional foundations.

In 2018, Navarro joined CityLink Community Services, a larger nonprofit organization that operated across several districts. At CityLink, Navarro continued to serve as a Nonprofit Program Manager, with responsibility for a portfolio of education and health access programs. Their duties included writing program plans, preparing annual budgets, coordinating staff schedules, and reporting results to the executive director and board of directors. Navarro also collaborated with municipal agencies on shared initiatives.

One of Navarro's key projects at CityLink was the "Neighborhood Learning Hubs" initiative, which created small study spaces inside apartment complexes and community centers. As Nonprofit Program Manager, Navarro coordinated the installation of computers, arranged for internet access, and organized volunteer tutors. They worked with property managers, librarians, and school counselors to identify suitable locations and recruit participants. The program targeted middle school students who lacked quiet places to study at home.

Navarro also managed a basic health access program known as "CheckUp Corners." This program set up monthly health information tables in markets and bus stations. As Nonprofit Program Manager, Navarro arranged for nurses and health educators to provide blood pressure checks, information on local clinics, and referrals to low-cost services. They oversaw the creation of multilingual brochures and developed procedures for collecting anonymous data about visitors' needs.

In addition to direct program oversight, Navarro has been involved in organizational capacity-building efforts. They led internal training sessions on data collection methods, project management software, and volunteer supervision. Navarro helped design a standard program manual used by multiple departments within CityLink Community Services. This manual included templates for work plans, risk assessments, and evaluation forms.

Navarro is known within their organizations for emphasizing measurable results and clear communication. As a Nonprofit Program Manager, they regularly prepare logic models, progress reports, and annual summaries for funders. They have coordinated external evaluations that use surveys, focus groups, and school records to assess program outcomes. Navarro has also presented program findings at regional conferences for nonprofit professionals and city planners.

Outside of their formal duties, Navarro participates in professional networks for Nonprofit Program Managers and related roles. They attend workshops on grant compliance, equity in service delivery, and trauma-informed practices. Navarro has contributed to working groups that develop shared standards for youth program quality across multiple organizations in the region. They also mentor early-career staff who are interested in program management positions.

Navarro lives in an apartment near Harbor Point's central transit hub. They commute to various program sites using public transportation and sometimes a shared bicycle system. Navarro often visits schools, community centers, and partner agencies as part of their responsibilities as a Nonprofit Program Manager. Their schedule includes regular evening meetings with community advisory groups and periodic weekend events.

Future plans for Navarro's career center on expanding the scale and coordination of nonprofit programs. They have expressed, in internal planning documents, an interest in developing citywide frameworks that align after-school programs, health access services, and digital literacy initiatives. As a Nonprofit Program Manager, Navarro continues to focus on building structured, replicable models that can be adapted by other organizations and municipalities. Their work remains concentrated on improving access to education and basic health resources for residents of Harbor Point and surrounding areas.
